o1.biggest_strength: It is built tightly on the conversion data, correctly shifts capacity away from decaying blog work, and gives the writer a usable first-week plan.
o1.biggest_mistake: Some upside estimates are optimistic and use comparison-page conversion rates for pages that may not behave like comparison pages.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Use more conservative ranges for forecasts and move the cookie-banner/no-cookies rewrite into the first week alongside the Fathom brief.

o2.biggest_strength: It makes the right strategic call in plain language, uses trial-rate math well, and gives a very actionable Monday-to-Friday writing plan with ready-to-use title and meta copy.
o2.biggest_mistake: The stop list says to leave old posts unchanged, which misses the opportunity to consolidate or redirect decaying posts into higher-converting pages.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a light consolidation/redirect plan for weak blog posts and bring the cookie-banner and no-cookies page work into week one.

reason: Both are strong and usable, but Output 2 is a little more credible on forecasts, clearer on capacity, and has more immediately paste-ready first-week copy. Output 1 has a better consolidation idea, but its projections are more aggressive.
